claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1i,j,m.

claims.claim: Expression of dnmt3bb.1 is strongly reduced in Notch-deficient mindbomb (mib) mutants.
claims.source: Similarly, expression of dnmt3bb.1 is also strongly reduced in Notch-deficient mindbomb (mib) mutants (Figure 1k,l,m).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1k,l,m.

claims.claim: dnmt3bb.1 is expressed by developing HSPCs downstream from the established Notch-Runx1 pathway for HSPC specification.
claims.source: These results show that dnmt3bb.1 is expressed by developing HSPCs downstream from the established Notch-Runx1 pathway for HSPC specification (Burns et al., 2005; Chen et al., 2009; Kissa and Herbomel, 2010), and that its expression is lost when HSPCs are not properly specified.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing dnmt3bb.1 expression is regulated by Notch and Runx1, combined with citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: dnmt3bb.1 expression is lost when HSPCs are not properly specified.
claims.source: These results show that dnmt3bb.1 is expressed by developing HSPCs downstream from the established Notch-Runx1 pathway for HSPC specification (Burns et al., 2005; Chen et al., 2009; Kissa and Herbomel, 2010), and that its expression is lost when HSPCs are not properly specified.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that dnmt3bb.1 expression is reduced in runx1 and mib mutants where HSPCs are not properly specified.

claims.claim: A dnmt3bb.1y258 mutant allele encodes a polypeptide prematurely truncated at amino acid 172 (P166fs) due to an 11 nucleotide deletion.
claims.source: We obtained a dnmt3bb.1y258 mutant allele encoding a polypeptide prematurely truncated at amino acid 172 (P166fs) due to an 11 nucleotide deletion (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a–e).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by molecular characterization data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1a–e.

claims.claim: Two to five dpf dnmt3bb.1y258 mutants are morphologically indistinguishable from their wild-type siblings.
claims.source: Morphologically, two to five dpf dnmt3bb.1y258 mutants are indistinguishable from their wild-type siblings (Figure 2a,b).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by transmitted light images shown in Figure 2a,b.

claims.claim: At 36 hpf, cmyb expression in HSPCs in the ventral aorta is similar in dnmt3bb.1y258 mutant embryos and their wild type siblings.
claims.source: At 36 hpf, cmyb expression in HSPCs in the ventral aorta is similar in dnmt3bb.1y258 mutant embryos and their wild type siblings (Figure 2c,d).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2c,d.

claims.claim: By 72 and 96 hpf cmyb expression is strongly reduced in the caudal hematopoietic tissue (CHT) of dnmt3bb.1y258 mutants.
claims.source: However, by 72 and 96 hpf cmyb expression is strongly reduced in the caudal hematopoietic tissue (CHT) of dnmt3bb.1y258 mutants (Figure 2e–h), as confirmed by genotyping of blindly scored embryos (Figure 2—figure supplement 1e).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2e–h and genotyping data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1e.

claims.claim: Loss of cmyb is accompanied by strong reduction in myeloid marker l-plastin in the CHT at 72 hpf in dnmt3bb.1y258 mutants.
claims.source: Loss of cmyb is also accompanied by strong reduction in myeloid marker l-plastin (Herbomel et al., 1999) in the CHT at 72 hpf (Figure 2i,j) and lymphoid marker rag1 (Willett et al., 1997) in the 5 dpf thymus (Figure 2k,l).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2i,j and citation.

claims.claim: Loss of cmyb is accompanied by strong reduction in lymphoid marker rag1 in the 5 dpf thymus in dnmt3bb.1y258 mutants.
claims.source: Loss of cmyb is also accompanied by strong reduction in myeloid marker l-plastin (Herbomel et al., 1999) in the CHT at 72 hpf (Figure 2i,j) and lymphoid marker rag1 (Willett et al., 1997) in the 5 dpf thymus (Figure 2k,l).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2k,l and citation.

claims.claim: Wild type embryos injected with dnmt3bb.1-targeting morpholinos show progressive loss of cmyb expression.
claims.source: We observed similar hematopoietic defects in wild type embryos injected with any one of three different dnmt3bb.1-targeting morpholinos, with progressive loss of cmyb expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a–f) as well as reduced expression of l-plastin (Figure 2—figure supplement 2g,i) and erythroid marker gata1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2k–n) in the 72 hpf CHT, and reduced expression of rag1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2h,j), ikaros, and lck:gfp (Figure 2—figure supplement 2o–r) in the 5 dpf thymus.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2a–f.

claims.claim: Wild type embryos injected with dnmt3bb.1-targeting morpholinos show reduced expression of l-plastin in the 72 hpf CHT.
claims.source: We observed similar hematopoietic defects in wild type embryos injected with any one of three different dnmt3bb.1-targeting morpholinos, with progressive loss of cmyb expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a–f) as well as reduced expression of l-plastin (Figure 2—figure supplement 2g,i) and erythroid marker gata1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2k–n) in the 72 hpf CHT, and reduced expression of rag1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2h,j), ikaros, and lck:gfp (Figure 2—figure supplement 2o–r) in the 5 dpf thymus.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2g,i.

claims.claim: Wild type embryos injected with dnmt3bb.1-targeting morpholinos show reduced expression of erythroid marker gata1 in the 72 hpf CHT.
claims.source: We observed similar hematopoietic defects in wild type embryos injected with any one of three different dnmt3bb.1-targeting morpholinos, with progressive loss of cmyb expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a–f) as well as reduced expression of l-plastin (Figure 2—figure supplement 2g,i) and erythroid marker gata1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2k–n) in the 72 hpf CHT, and reduced expression of rag1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2h,j), ikaros, and lck:gfp (Figure 2—figure supplement 2o–r) in the 5 dpf thymus.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2k–n.

claims.claim: Wild type embryos injected with dnmt3bb.1-targeting morpholinos show reduced expression of rag1, ikaros, and lck:gfp in the 5 dpf thymus.
claims.source: We observed similar hematopoietic defects in wild type embryos injected with any one of three different dnmt3bb.1-targeting morpholinos, with progressive loss of cmyb expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a–f) as well as reduced expression of l-plastin (Figure 2—figure supplement 2g,i) and erythroid marker gata1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2k–n) in the 72 hpf CHT, and reduced expression of rag1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2h,j), ikaros, and lck:gfp (Figure 2—figure supplement 2o–r) in the 5 dpf thymus.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2h,j,o–r.

claims.claim: Quantitative RT-PCR confirmed progressive loss of cmyb and strong reduction in subsequent l-plastin and rag1 expression in Dnmt3bb.1-deficient animals.
claims.source: Quantitative RT-PCR confirmed progressive loss of cmyb and strong reduction in subsequent l-plastin and rag1 expression in Dnmt3bb.1-deficient animals (Figure 2m,n).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2m,n.

claims.claim: Strong increase in active caspase 3 in HSPC in the trunks of 48 hpf Dnmt3bb.1-deficient animals indicated that HSPCs are undergoing apoptosis.
claims.source: Strong increase in active caspase 3 in HSPC in the trunks of 48 hpf Dnmt3bb.1-deficient animals indicated that HSPCs are undergoing apoptosis (Figure 2—figure supplement 3a–c).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical staining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3a–c.

claims.claim: Despite dramatic hematopoietic defects, Dnmt3bb.1-deficient animals appeared otherwise unaffected, with normal vascular patterning and vascular gene expression.
claims.source: Despite dramatic hematopoietic defects, Dnmt3bb.1-deficient animals appeared otherwise unaffected, with normal vascular patterning and vascular gene expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 3d–i).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by transmitted light images, confocal images, and in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3d–i.

claims.claim: Loss of dnmt3bb.1 activity leads to a specific defect in HSPCs, with progressive loss of cmyb expression and decreased numbers of HSPCs.
claims.source: These results suggest that loss of dnmt3bb.1 activity leads to a specific defect in HSPCs, with progressive loss of cmyb expression and decreased numbers of HSPCs.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion inferred from the multiple experimental results showing HSPC-specific defects in dnmt3bb.1-deficient animals.

claims.claim: RNAseq analysis showed that the expression of a variety of hematopoietic genes was reduced in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs.
claims.source: RNAseq analysis (and subsequent qPCR validation of selected genes) showed that the expression of a variety of hematopoietic genes was reduced in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs, while many endothelial and apoptosis pathway genes were increased relative to control HSPCs (Figure 3b,c, Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by RNAseq data shown in Figure 3b,c and Figure 3—figure supplement 1b.

claims.claim: Many endothelial and apoptosis pathway genes were increased in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs relative to control HSPCs.
claims.source: RNAseq analysis (and subsequent qPCR validation of selected genes) showed that the expression of a variety of hematopoietic genes was reduced in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs, while many endothelial and apoptosis pathway genes were increased relative to control HSPCs (Figure 3b,c, Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by RNAseq data shown in Figure 3b,c and Figure 3—figure supplement 1b.

claims.claim: Ingenuity pathway analysis confirmed elevated VEGF/angiogenesis and apoptosis pathway gene expression indicating lack of endothelial to hematopoietic transition and induction of apoptosis in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs.
claims.source: Ingenuity pathway analysis (www.qiagen.com/ingenuity) confirmed elevated VEGF/angiogenesis and apoptosis pathway gene expression indicating lack of endothelial to hematopoietic transition and induction of apoptosis in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs (Figure 3d).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Ingenuity pathway analysis results shown in Figure 3d.

claims.claim: Very few of the hematopoietic or endothelial genes with significantly altered expression displayed significantly decreased DNA methylation in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs.
claims.source: However, RRBS analysis revealed that very few of the hematopoietic or endothelial genes with significantly altered expression displayed significantly decreased DNA methylation (Figure 3—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by RRBS analysis results.

claims.claim: cmyb was one of the most affected and highly correlated of the hematopoietic genes that showed both significantly reduced expression in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs and significantly reduced methylation of an adjacent promoter or gene body CpG island.
claims.source: cmyb was one of the most affected and highly correlated of the hematopoietic genes that showed both significantly reduced expression in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs and significantly reduced methylation of an adjacent promoter or gene body CpG island (Figure 3e, Figure 3—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by combined RRBS and RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 3e.

claims.claim: Direct sequencing of PCR-amplified fragments from bisulfite treated DNA confirmed reduced methylation in the cmyb intron 1 CpG island in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs.
claims.source: Direct sequencing of PCR-amplified fragments from bisulfite treated DNA confirmed reduced methylation in the cmyb intron 1 CpG island in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs (Figure 3f), but no change in the runx1 exon 3 CpG island (Figure 3g), or in CpG islands from a number of other hematopoietic and endothelial genes showing significantly altered expression in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPC (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c,d).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 3f.

claims.claim: There was no change in methylation of the runx1 exon 3 CpG island in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs.
claims.source: Direct sequencing of PCR-amplified fragments from bisulfite treated DNA confirmed reduced methylation in the cmyb intron 1 CpG island in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs (Figure 3f), but no change in the runx1 exon 3 CpG island (Figure 3g), or in CpG islands from a number of other hematopoietic and endothelial genes showing significantly altered expression in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPC (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c,d).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 3g.

claims.claim: There was no change in methylation of CpG islands from a number of other hematopoietic and endothelial genes showing significantly altered expression in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPC.
claims.source: Direct sequencing of PCR-amplified fragments from bisulfite treated DNA confirmed reduced methylation in the cmyb intron 1 CpG island in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs (Figure 3f), but no change in the runx1 exon 3 CpG island (Figure 3g), or in CpG islands from a number of other hematopoietic and endothelial genes showing significantly altered expression in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPC (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c,d).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1c,d.

claims.claim: cmyb is a target of dnmt3bb.1-mediated regulation in HSPCs.
claims.source: These results suggest that cmyb is a target of dnmt3bb.1-mediated regulation in HSPCs.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the combined RRBS and RNAseq data showing cmyb has both reduced methylation and reduced expression in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs.

claims.claim: 319 genes were identified whose expression in blood had been confirmed by in situ staining or PCR.
claims.source: Genes expressed by blood cells were identified in the ZFIN zebrafish gene expression database (http://zfin.org/cgi-bin/webdriver?MIval=aa-ZDB_home.apg) using search terms blood, HSCs, ventral wall of dorsal aorta, and all associated search terms. 319 genes were identified whose expression in blood had been confirmed by in situ staining or PCR.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on a database search and analysis described in the methods.

claims.claim: 57 of the 319 hematopoietic genes were found to have a total of 72 CpG islands in their gene bodies.
claims.source: Each of these 319 gene loci were then further analyzed using the UCSC genome browser or WashU epigenetics browser to determine whether there were CpG islands in their gene bodies. The gene body was defined as 5'UTR, all exons and introns and 3' UTR. 57 genes with 72 CpG islands in their gene bodies were identified.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on computational analysis of gene structures.

claims.claim: 10 of the 72 CpG islands are methylated in blood cells.
claims.source: We carried out bisulfite restriction analysis to determine whether these 72 CpG islands are methylated in blood cells, using genomic DNA isolated from circulating blood cells obtained after amputating the tails of 5–7-day-old zebrafish (Figure 4a), and determined that 10 of the 72 CpG islands are methylated in blood cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite restriction analysis described in the text and Figure 4a.

claims.claim: Only the cmyb intron 1 CpG island showed dnmt3bb.1-dependent changes in methylation among the 10 methylated CpG islands.
claims.source: To determine whether methylation of these CpG islands was dnmt3bb.1-dependent, we carried out bisulfite sequencing on each of the 10 methylated CpG islands using 5 dpf blood cell genomic DNA isolated from either control or dnmt3bb.1 morpholino-injected zebrafish. Only one CpG island showed dnmt3bb.1-dependent changes in methylation, the cmyb intron 1 CpG island (Figure 4b).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 4b.

claims.claim: No change was detected in the methylation of the runx1 exon 3 CpG island in dnmt3bb.1-deficient blood cells.
claims.source: No change was detected in the methylation of the runx1 exon 3 CpG island (Figure 4c), or in any of the other eight hematopoietic genes containing methylated CpG islands in blood cells (Figure 4d–k).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 4c.

claims.claim: No change was detected in the methylation of any of the other eight hematopoietic genes containing methylated CpG islands in blood cells in dnmt3bb.1-deficient animals.
claims.source: No change was detected in the methylation of the runx1 exon 3 CpG island (Figure 4c), or in any of the other eight hematopoietic genes containing methylated CpG islands in blood cells (Figure 4d–k).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 4d–k.

claims.claim: cmyb is a key proximal hematopoietic target of dnmt3bb.1.
claims.source: These results support the findings of our RRBS analysis above, suggesting that cmyb is a key proximal hematopoietic target of dnmt3bb.1.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the genome-wide screen showing only cmyb CpG island methylation is dnmt3bb.1-dependent.

claims.claim: Dnmt3bb.1-GFP-positive cells were consistently also cmyb positive in Tol2(kdrl:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected animals.
claims.source: In Tol2(kdrl:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected animals Dnmt3bb.1-GFP-positive cells were consistently also cmyb positive, and double–positive cells were found throughout the vasculature, not only in their normal location in the trunk (Figure 5b,c,d), but also in ectopic locations such as the cranial vasculature (Figure 5b,e,f).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by double in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 5b,c,d,e,f.

claims.claim: Double-positive cells were found throughout the vasculature, not only in their normal location in the trunk, but also in ectopic locations such as the cranial vasculature in Tol2(kdrl:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected animals.
claims.source: In Tol2(kdrl:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected animals Dnmt3bb.1-GFP-positive cells were consistently also cmyb positive, and double–positive cells were found throughout the vasculature, not only in their normal location in the trunk (Figure 5b,c,d), but also in ectopic locations such as the cranial vasculature (Figure 5b,e,f).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by double in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 5b,c,d,e,f.

claims.claim: Forced expression of dnmt3bb.1 can promote cmyb expression in endothelial cells even in the absence of runx1 function.
claims.source: We observed similar induction of cmyb expression in dnmt3bb.1-gfp expressing cells when the transgene was injected into runx1 mutant animals lacking endogenous cmyb expression in HSPCs (Figure 5b,g,h), showing that the forced expression of dnmt3bb.1 can promote cmyb expression in endothelial cells even in the absence of runx1 function.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by double in situ hybridization data in runx1 mutants shown in Figure 5b,g,h.

claims.claim: Heat shocked animals expressing Dnmt3bb.1-GFP fusion protein from the injected Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene showed robust mosaic expression of cmyb, rag1, and l-plastin.
claims.source: In contrast, heat shocked animals expressing Dnmt3bb.1-GFP fusion protein from the injected Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene showed robust mosaic expression of cmyb, rag1, and l-plastin (Figure 6f-h,k).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6f-h,k.

claims.claim: Dnmt3bb.1-GFP-injected embryos also express lymphoid markers ikaros and rag2, as well as hemoglobin ae1 (hbae1), a marker of both primitive and definitive erythroid cells.
claims.source: Dnmt3bb.1-GFP-injected embryos also express lymphoid markers ikaros and rag2, as well as hemoglobin ae1 (hbae1), a marker of both primitive and definitive erythroid cells (Jin et al., 2009), showing induction of erythroid lineage genes also occurs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1a–h), but they do not express endothelial markers cadherin 5 (cdh5) and ets-related protein (etsrp, also known as etv2) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1i–l).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1a–h and citation.

claims.claim: Dnmt3bb.1-GFP-injected embryos do not express endothelial markers cadherin 5 (cdh5) and ets-related protein (etsrp, also known as etv2).
claims.source: Dnmt3bb.1-GFP-injected embryos also express lymphoid markers ikaros and rag2, as well as hemoglobin ae1 (hbae1), a marker of both primitive and definitive erythroid cells (Jin et al., 2009), showing induction of erythroid lineage genes also occurs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1a–h), but they do not express endothelial markers cadherin 5 (cdh5) and ets-related protein (etsrp, also known as etv2) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1i–l).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1i–l.

claims.claim: dnmt3bb.1 specifically promotes hematopoietic development without inducing mesoderm, endothelial precursors, or 'hemangioblasts'.
claims.source: This suggests that dnmt3bb.1 specifically promotes hematopoietic development without inducing mesoderm, endothelial precursors, or 'hemangioblasts'.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the observation that dnmt3bb.1 overexpression induces hematopoietic markers but not endothelial markers.

claims.claim: 17/30 (57%) of the host animals that received cells from heat shocked Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) donors showed donor cells homing to the thymus.
claims.source: On day 5, 17/30 (57%) of the host animals that received cells from heat shocked Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) donors showed donor cells (red fluorescent, rhodamine/biotin-dextran-labeled) homing to the thymus, as compared to only 11/38 (29%) of host animals that received cells from control heat -shocked Tol2(hsp70:gfp) donors (Figure 6n–q).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by transplantation experiment data shown in Figure 6n–q.

claims.claim: Only 11/38 (29%) of host animals that received cells from control heat-shocked Tol2(hsp70:gfp) donors showed donor cells homing to the thymus.
claims.source: On day 5, 17/30 (57%) of the host animals that received cells from heat shocked Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) donors showed donor cells (red fluorescent, rhodamine/biotin-dextran-labeled) homing to the thymus, as compared to only 11/38 (29%) of host animals that received cells from control heat -shocked Tol2(hsp70:gfp) donors (Figure 6n–q).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by transplantation experiment data shown in Figure 6n–q.

claims.claim: The thymus-positive dnmt3bb.1-gfp transplanted hosts had approximately twice as many cells in the thymus compared to the thymus-positive gfp control transplanted hosts.
claims.source: The thymus-positive dnmt3bb.1-gfp transplanted hosts had approximately twice as many cells in the thymus compared to the thymus-positive gfp control transplanted hosts, while the number of intravenously injected cells that were lodged non-specifically in the heart and aortic arches was comparable.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitation of transplanted cells shown in Figure 6q.

claims.claim: The number of intravenously injected cells that were lodged non-specifically in the heart and aortic arches was comparable between dnmt3bb.1-gfp and control gfp transplanted hosts.
claims.source: The thymus-positive dnmt3bb.1-gfp transplanted hosts had approximately twice as many cells in the thymus compared to the thymus-positive gfp control transplanted hosts, while the number of intravenously injected cells that were lodged non-specifically in the heart and aortic arches was comparable.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitation of transplanted cells shown in Figure 6q.

claims.claim: Bisulfite sequencing reveals that the cmyb intron 1 CpG island becomes methylated in DNA from heat-shocked mosaic Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected shield stage animals.
claims.source: Bisulfite sequencing reveals that the cmyb intron 1 CpG island becomes methylated in DNA from heat -shocked mosaic Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected shield stage animals, but not in DNA from heat shocked control Tol2(hsp70:gfp) transgene-injected animals (Figure 7a).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 7a.

claims.claim: The cmyb intron 1 CpG island does not become methylated in DNA from heat shocked control Tol2(hsp70:gfp) transgene-injected animals.
claims.source: Bisulfite sequencing reveals that the cmyb intron 1 CpG island becomes methylated in DNA from heat -shocked mosaic Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected shield stage animals, but not in DNA from heat shocked control Tol2(hsp70:gfp) transgene-injected animals (Figure 7a).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 7a.

claims.claim: A separate cmyb 5' CpG island that is not normally methylated in HSPC in wild type animals does not become ectopically methylated in heat-shocked Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected shield stage animals.
claims.source: A separate cmyb 5' CpG island that is not normally methylated in HSPC in wild type animals does not become ectopically methylated in heat-shocked Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected shield stage animals (Figure 7b).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 7b.

claims.claim: Chromatin immunoprecipitation shows that dnmt3bb.1-GFP binds to two independent DNA sequences from the cmyb intron 1 CpG island.
claims.source: Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) of DNA from heat-shocked Tol2(hsp70:gfp) or Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected or Tg(hsp70:tcf-gfp) germline transgenic (Lewis et al., 2004) shield-stage animals (Figure 7c) using anti-GFP antibodies shows that dnmt3bb.1-GFP (but not Tcf-GFP) binds to two independent DNA sequences from the cmyb intron 1 CpG island (Figure 7d, rows 1 and 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 7d, rows 1 and 2.

claims.claim: Dnmt3bb.1-GFP does not bind to non-CpG island cmyb DNA from intron 1 or exon 5, or to CpG island DNA from the runx1 or ntla gene loci.
claims.source: Dnmt3bb.1-GFP does not bind to non-CpG island cmyb DNA from intron 1 or exon 5, or to CpG island DNA from the runx1 or ntla gene loci (Figure 7d, rows 3–6).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 7d, rows 3–6.

claims.claim: Tcf-GFP shows specific association with sox3 DNA sequences containing known TCF binding sites.
claims.source: As an additional ChIP control, Tcf-GFP (but not Dnmt3bb.1-gfp) shows specific association with sox3 DNA sequences containing known TCF binding sites (Lee et al., 2006) (Figure 7d, row 7), but does not associate with any dnmt3bb.1 DNA sequence.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 7d, row 7 and citation.

claims.claim: ChIP using anti-methyl cytosine confirms methylation of the cmyb intron 1 CpG island in animals expressing dnmt3bb.1-GFP but not GFP alone.
claims.source: ChIP using anti-methyl cytosine (Figure 7e) confirms methylation of the cmyb intron 1 CpG island in animals expressing dnmt3bb.1-GFP but not GFP alone (Figure 7e, rows 1 and 2), as well as 'constitutive' methylation of the runx1 and ntla CpG islands (Figure 7e, rows 5 and 6).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 7e, rows 1 and 2.

claims.claim: ChIP using anti-methyl cytosine shows 'constitutive' methylation of the runx1 and ntla CpG islands.
claims.source: ChIP using anti-methyl cytosine (Figure 7e) confirms methylation of the cmyb intron 1 CpG island in animals expressing dnmt3bb.1-GFP but not GFP alone (Figure 7e, rows 1 and 2), as well as 'constitutive' methylation of the runx1 and ntla CpG islands (Figure 7e, rows 5 and 6).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 7e, rows 5 and 6.

claims.claim: Dnmt3bb.1 methylates the cmyb intron 1 CpG island to maintain the expression of cmyb in HSPCs.
claims.source: Together, these results suggest that Dnmt3bb.1 methylates the cmyb intron 1 CpG island to maintain the expression of cmyb in HSPCs, and that loss of Dnmt3bb.1 results in failure to maintain cmyb expression and loss of HSPCs.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the combined bisulfite sequencing and ChIP data showing dnmt3bb.1 binds to and methylates the cmyb intron 1 CpG island.

claims.claim: Loss of Dnmt3bb.1 results in failure to maintain cmyb expression and loss of HSPCs.
claims.source: Together, these results suggest that Dnmt3bb.1 methylates the cmyb intron 1 CpG island to maintain the expression of cmyb in HSPCs, and that loss of Dnmt3bb.1 results in failure to maintain cmyb expression and loss of HSPCs.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the combined loss-of-function and molecular data.

claims.claim: 10–12% of homozygous dnmt3bb.1 mutants survive to adulthood.
claims.source: In a similar fashion, we find that 10–12% of homozygous dnmt3bb.1 mutants also survive to adulthood (Figure 8a,b), and the anterior kidneys in these surviving mutants also exhibit severely reduced hematopoietic cellularity (Figure 8c–f).

claims.claim: DNA methylation-mediated epigenetic modifications downstream from Runx1 help maintain HSPC fate during definitive hematopoiesis.
claims.source: Our results highlight an important new role for DNA methyltransferases during the earliest stages of HSPC emergence in the developing embryo. The molecular mechanisms involved in generation and maintenance of HSPC from hemogenic endothelium are still not well understood, and our findings provide evidence that DNA methylation-mediated epigenetic modifications downstream from Runx1 help maintain HSPC fate during definitive hematopoiesis.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the experimental data.

results.result: dnmt3bb.1, the zebrafish ortholog of mammalian DNMT3B, is specifically expressed in cmyb-positive HSPCs in the ventral floor of the dorsal aorta at 36 hpf. The gene shows co-expression with the HSPC marker cmyb and is also expressed in some head tissues including the eye.
results.evaluation: Claims C28-C35 and C106 are well-supported by in situ hybridization data (Figure 1a-f), phylogenetic analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a), and double WISH confirming co-expression with cmyb. The spatial and temporal expression pattern is clearly documented with appropriate controls and imaging.

results.result: dnmt3bb.1 expression is regulated by the Notch-Runx1 pathway. Expression is reduced in runx1 morphants, runx1 mutants, and Notch-deficient mindbomb mutants, while runx1 overexpression increases dnmt3bb.1 expression in the axial vasculature.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C36-C40, C108-C109, and C111 are supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data (Figure 1h-m) showing consistent changes in dnmt3bb.1 expression following genetic manipulation of the Notch-Runx1 pathway. Multiple independent approaches (morpholinos, mutants, mRNA overexpression) provide converging evidence.

results.result: Loss of dnmt3bb.1 function leads to progressive loss of HSPCs and hematopoietic lineages. dnmt3bb.1y258 mutants show normal cmyb expression at 36 hpf but strongly reduced expression by 72-96 hpf, accompanied by reduced expression of myeloid (l-plastin), lymphoid (rag1, ikaros, lck), and erythroid (gata1) markers. Similar defects are observed with morpholino knockdown.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C52 and C115-C117 are well-supported by multiple lines of evidence including genetic mutant characterization (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), in situ hybridization at multiple time points (Figure 2c-l), morpholino validation (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), and qRT-PCR quantification (Figure 2m,n). The progressive nature of the defect is clearly documented with appropriate genotyping controls.

results.result: dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs undergo apoptosis while other developmental processes remain normal. Increased active caspase 3 is detected in HSPCs at 48 hpf, but vascular patterning and gene expression are unaffected.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C54 are supported by immunohistochemical staining showing increased caspase3 in cmyb:GFP+ cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 3a-c) with statistical significance (p=0.0012), and by confocal imaging and in situ hybridization showing normal vascular development (Figure 2—figure supplement 3d-i). This demonstrates specificity of the hematopoietic defect.

results.result: Combined RNAseq and RRBS analysis of FACS-isolated HSPCs reveals that while many hematopoietic genes show altered expression in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs, very few show corresponding changes in DNA methylation. cmyb is identified as one of the most significant genes showing both reduced expression and reduced methylation of its intron 1 CpG island.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C61, C129-C130 are supported by genome-wide RNAseq and RRBS data from FACS-sorted HSPCs (Figure 3a-e), with validation by qRT-PCR and targeted bisulfite sequencing (Figure 3f). The integration of expression and methylation data provides strong evidence for cmyb as a key target, though the analysis would benefit from more detailed statistical reporting of the correlation.

results.result: Other hematopoietic and endothelial genes showing altered expression in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs do not show changes in CpG island methylation, including runx1, gata2, scl, ikaros, lck, rag1, l-plastin, pu.1, and several endothelial markers.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C63 and C131 are supported by bisulfite sequencing data (Figure 3g, Figure 3—figure supplement 1c,d) showing no methylation changes in these genes despite altered expression. This specificity strengthens the case for cmyb as the primary direct target of dnmt3bb.1.

results.result: An unbiased genome-wide screen of 319 hematopoietic genes identified only 10 with methylated gene body CpG islands in blood cells. Of these, only the cmyb intron 1 CpG island shows dnmt3bb.1-dependent methylation changes.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C70 and C133-C135 are supported by systematic bisulfite restriction analysis and sequencing (Figure 4). The comprehensive screen provides strong evidence for cmyb as the primary hematopoietic target. However, the screen is limited to gene body CpG islands and may miss other regulatory regions.

results.result: Pan-endothelial overexpression of dnmt3bb.1 using the kdrl promoter induces ectopic cmyb expression throughout the vasculature, including in cranial vessels. This induction occurs even in runx1 mutants lacking endogenous cmyb expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C74 are supported by double in situ hybridization data (Figure 5b-h) showing co-expression of dnmt3bb.1-gfp and cmyb in both normal and ectopic locations, including in runx1 mutant backgrounds. This demonstrates sufficiency of dnmt3bb.1 to induce cmyb expression independent of runx1.

results.result: Heat shock-induced overexpression of dnmt3bb.1 in early blastula embryos (3 hpf) induces expression of multiple hematopoietic lineage markers (cmyb, rag1, l-plastin, ikaros, rag2, hbae1) by 6 hpf, but does not induce endothelial markers (cdh5, etsrp).
results.evaluation: Claims C75-C77, C120-C121 are supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data (Figure 6c-k, Figure 6—figure supplement 1) showing robust induction of hematopoietic markers but not endothelial markers. The timing (before normal HSPC emergence) and specificity (hematopoietic but not endothelial) are well-documented.

results.result: Transplantation experiments show that cells from dnmt3bb.1-overexpressing blastulae home to the thymus more frequently (57% vs 29%) and in greater numbers (~2-fold) than control cells, while non-specific lodging in heart/aortic arches is comparable.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C82 are supported by transplantation data (Figure 6n-q) with clear quantification. The increased thymus homing suggests functional HSPC properties. However, the statistical significance of the frequency difference is not reported, and the experiment would be strengthened by longer-term tracking and functional assays.

results.result: Bisulfite sequencing shows that the cmyb intron 1 CpG island becomes methylated in heat-shocked dnmt3bb.1-gfp transgene-injected embryos but not in control gfp-injected embryos. A separate cmyb 5' CpG island that is not normally methylated does not become ectopically methylated.
results.evaluation: Claims C83-C85 are supported by bisulfite sequencing data (Figure 7a,b) showing specific methylation of the intron 1 CpG island but not the 5' CpG island. This demonstrates specificity of dnmt3bb.1 targeting and rules out non-specific methylation.

results.result: Chromatin immunoprecipitation with anti-GFP antibodies shows that dnmt3bb.1-GFP specifically binds to two independent sequences within the cmyb intron 1 CpG island, but not to non-CpG island regions of cmyb or to CpG islands from runx1 or ntla genes.
results.evaluation: Claims C86-C88, C136-C137 are supported by ChIP data (Figure 7c,d) with appropriate positive (Tcf-GFP binding to sox3) and negative controls. The specificity of binding to the cmyb intron 1 CpG island is well-demonstrated, though quantification of enrichment would strengthen the result.

results.result: ChIP with anti-methyl cytosine antibodies confirms methylation of the cmyb intron 1 CpG island in dnmt3bb.1-GFP expressing embryos but not in GFP-only controls, and also shows constitutive methylation of runx1 and ntla CpG islands.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C90 and C138 are supported by ChIP data (Figure 7e) confirming that the cmyb intron 1 CpG island is specifically methylated in a dnmt3bb.1-dependent manner. The detection of constitutive methylation at other loci serves as a positive control for the antibody.

results.result: A small proportion (10-12%) of dnmt3bb.1 mutants survive to adulthood with severely reduced hematopoietic cellularity in the anterior kidney, malformed erythrocytes, and abnormal HSPC morphology. These phenotypes closely resemble those of cmyb mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C93-C97, C147-C148 are supported by analysis of adult mutants including histology (Figure 8c-f), blood smears (Figure 8g-i), and Giemsa staining of sorted HSPCs (Figure 8j,k). The similarity to published cmyb mutant phenotypes (cited) strengthens the conclusion that dnmt3bb.1 acts through cmyb.

results.result: Heat shock-induced overexpression of cmyb in early blastula embryos induces expression of hematopoietic lineage markers (hbae1, rag1, l-plastin, ikaros, lck, rag2) but not endothelial markers (cdh5, etsrp), similar to dnmt3bb.1 overexpression.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C100 and C149 are supported by in situ hybridization data (Figure 8—figure supplement 1) showing that cmyb overexpression phenocopies dnmt3bb.1 overexpression. This supports the model that dnmt3bb.1 acts through cmyb to induce hematopoietic gene expression.

results.result: Co-injection of dnmt3bb.1-gfp transgene with cmyb morpholino dramatically reduces l-plastin and rag1 expression compared to dnmt3bb.1-gfp alone, demonstrating that cmyb is necessary for dnmt3bb.1-mediated hematopoietic gene expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C101, C150-C151 are supported by in situ hybridization data (Figure 6g-j) showing that cmyb knockdown blocks dnmt3bb.1-induced hematopoietic gene expression. This epistasis experiment provides strong evidence that cmyb functions downstream of dnmt3bb.1.

results.result: dnmt3bb.1 is essential for HSPC maintenance through an epigenetic mechanism involving methylation of the cmyb locus. Loss of dnmt3bb.1 leads to reduced cmyb methylation, reduced cmyb expression, and gradual loss of HSPCs, while dnmt3bb.1 overexpression is sufficient to methylate cmyb and promote hematopoietic development.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C3-C5, C91-C92, C152, C171 represent the central conclusion of the manuscript, supported by the integration of loss-of-function studies (mutants and morpholinos), gain-of-function studies (overexpression), molecular analysis (bisulfite sequencing, ChIP), and functional assays (transplantation). The evidence is comprehensive and internally consistent.

results.result: The study provides a mechanistic model explaining how transient Runx1 expression leads to sustained cmyb expression: Runx1 activates both cmyb and dnmt3bb.1 expression; dnmt3bb.1 then methylates the cmyb gene body to maintain cmyb expression after Runx1 is downregulated.
results.evaluation: Claims C153-C157 represent the mechanistic model illustrated in Figure 9. The model is well-supported by the experimental data showing: (1) Runx1 regulates dnmt3bb.1 expression, (2) cmyb is initially expressed normally in dnmt3bb.1 mutants at 36 hpf, (3) dnmt3bb.1 can induce cmyb even in runx1 mutants, and (4) dnmt3bb.1 methylates the cmyb locus. The model provides a coherent explanation for the data.

results.result: Ectopic overexpression of dnmt3bb.1 in non-hematopoietic cells is sufficient to methylate the cmyb locus, promote cmyb expression, and induce hematopoietic development.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C8 are supported by bisulfite sequencing (Figure 7a), in situ hybridization (Figure 6f-h), and expression of multiple hematopoietic markers (Figure 6—figure supplement 1). However, the claim of 'non-hematopoietic cells' in early blastulae is somewhat imprecise since these are naive cells before lineage specification.

results.result: cmyb is both necessary and sufficient for hematopoietic lineage gene expression, and is a key locus regulated by dnmt3bb.1 during hematopoietic differentiation. Hematopoietic genes cannot be induced by dnmt3bb.1 in the absence of cmyb.
results.evaluation: Claims C102-C104 and C128 are supported by the cmyb overexpression experiments (Figure 8—figure supplement 1) and the epistasis experiment showing cmyb knockdown blocks dnmt3bb.1-induced gene expression (Figure 6g-j). The comprehensive molecular and functional data support cmyb as the key target.

results.result: In contrast to DNMT3A-mediated promoter methylation and gene repression in neural crest specification, dnmt3bb.1 promotes HSPC maintenance through gene body (not promoter) methylation of cmyb, and cmyb expression is activated (not repressed) by DNA methylation.
results.evaluation: Claims C159-C160 are supported by the bisulfite sequencing data showing methylation specifically in the cmyb intron 1 (gene body) CpG island (Figure 3f, 4b, 7a) and the observation that loss of dnmt3bb.1 leads to reduced (not increased) cmyb expression. This represents an important mechanistic distinction from other DNMT3 family functions.

results.result: Background claims about HSPC development, the Notch-Runx1-Cmyb pathway, DNA methylation mechanisms, and DNMT function are established knowledge from prior studies.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C27, C30, C33, C107 represent established knowledge supported by appropriate citations to previous literature. These provide necessary context for the current study and are accurately represented.

results.result: Additional background claims about DNMT3B expression in mouse embryos, epigenetic regulation in other systems, and DNA methylation in hematopoiesis are supported by citations to previous studies.
results.evaluation: Claims C112-C113, C122, C126, C140-C144, C158, C161-C163, C165-C170, C172, C174 represent relevant background information from the literature, appropriately cited. These contextualize the current findings within the broader field.

results.result: Speculative claims about mechanisms and evolutionary conservation suggest that reduced dnmt3bb.1 expression in mutants may reflect reduced HSPC numbers rather than direct regulation, and that DNMT roles may be conserved in vertebrates.
results.evaluation: Claims C110, C114, C173 are explicitly speculative statements by the authors. C110 acknowledges an alternative interpretation of the runx1/mib mutant data. C114 and C173 suggest evolutionary conservation based on expression patterns but lack functional validation in other species. These are reasonable hypotheses but require further testing.

results.result: Speculative claims about the functional properties of dnmt3bb.1-overexpressing cells, the mechanism of hematopoietic conversion, and potential cooperating factors represent reasonable inferences but lack direct experimental validation.
results.evaluation: Claims C123-C125, C127, C145 represent inferences and speculation by the authors. C123 is supported by transplantation data but C124 is an inference. C125 and C127 are reasonable interpretations but alternative explanations are not fully excluded. C145 is explicit speculation about potential mechanisms. These would benefit from additional experimental validation.

results.result: The mechanisms targeting DNA methyltransferases to specific CpG islands are poorly understood.
results.evaluation: Claim C139 is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field, which is accurate based on the literature. This contextualizes the lack of mechanistic detail about dnmt3bb.1 targeting specificity in the current study.

results.result: Summary and interpretive claims synthesizing the experimental results to conclude that dnmt3bb.1 specifically targets cmyb to maintain HSPC fate.
results.evaluation: Claims C55, C64, C71, C78, C98, C105, C132, C146 are summary statements and interpretations that are well-supported by the collective experimental evidence. These represent reasonable conclusions from the data, though some (like C132) involve inference about genes not being direct targets based on lack of methylation changes.
